content.text:
I checked 16 claims against the record and flagged none. Every claim has support in the record.

- **Cause:** The root cause and the plain-words explanation are hedged ("unverified", "likely") and rest on F1, Code-Fix's reading of the source, so they don't overstate it.
- **First appearance of the error:** The claim that the ZeroDivisionError shows up first at the onset holds. The logs read go back 37 minutes before the alert (T11), and G5309 only starts at 02:55.
- **Partial-to-full rollout (contributing factor 4):** This follows from the log lines. At 02:55, 26 of 200 evaluations were on (G971b); from 02:56 every evaluation was on (Gce95).
- **"Still failing at escalation":** The logs only run to 03:02, but the record says the service was not back to normal by 03:04:19, which covers this claim.
- **Not judged:** The six action items and the "had it been otherwise" what-ifs. The one fact stated inside a what-if, that the flag was left for a person, is backed by T17.

supported.quote: With monthly-spend-feature on, `render_spend_summary` calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month` (as long as `use_typical_spend` is false). That function divides the account's total for this month by the number of its purchases marked `in_current_month`. A shopper who has bought before but not this month has none, so the division is by zero and their account page request raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.

A setting that adds a monthly spending summary to account pages came on, and nothing Argus read records who or what turned it on; the summary's code likely fails when it works out an average for shoppers who have bought before but bought nothing this month.

While monthly-spend-feature stayed on, account pages could keep failing for shoppers who had bought before but not this month, and the flag could be switched again without showing up in any change record Argus reads.
Account pages failed for some shoppers
The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. That error first appears in the logs at the onset and nowhere before it.

The monthly-spend-feature flag began evaluating on. Every evaluation logged during {G7e5d.4} was off. At {G971b.6} some evaluations were on, and the logs show it on during {Gce95.4}. The switch appears in no change record Argus read: the production change events returned {T9.2} changes, and the flag provider's history showed {T15.2} flag changes by anyone but Argus. What switched the flag is not in the record. No deploy or other change was recorded, so none could be ruled out by the service being measured healthy with it in place.
Turning the flag on sent account pages for shoppers with no purchases this month down a code path that divides by their number of purchases this month.
The switch of monthly-spend-feature to on was not recorded in the production change events or the flag provider's history, so Argus had no recorded change it could undo and refused to act on C1.
That would have stopped the failing account pages instead of leaving the flag on for a person to deal with.
The alert paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.

supported.quote: No test was seen that exercised the flag-gated monthly summary for a shopper who has bought before but not this month before the flag was turned on.
Code-Fix reports that the existing tests call this shopper the ordinary case and their own helper builds one.
The flag went from on for part of traffic to on for all of it, and no guard was seen that held or reverted it while the account page error rate rose.
Once Argus left undoing the flag to a person
No mitigation was applied during the response: the flag was still on and account pages were still failing when the incident was escalated to a person.
